8th circuit court of appeals

The 8th Circuit Court of Appeals is a federal court located in St. Louis, Missouri, with jurisdiction over the states of Arkansas, Iowa, Minnesota, Missouri, Nebraska, North Dakota, and South Dakota. The court has 11 judges and is one of 13 circuit courts in the United States. In this article, we will provide an overview of the 8th Circuit Court of Appeals, its history, jurisdiction, and notable cases.

History of the 8th Circuit Court of Appeals

The 8th Circuit Court of Appeals was established in 1891 as part of a major overhaul of the federal court system. At the time, the United States was divided into nine judicial circuits, each with a court of appeals. The 8th Circuit was created to hear cases from the newly admitted states of North Dakota, South Dakota, Nebraska, and Minnesota. Over the years, the court's jurisdiction has expanded to include Arkansas, Iowa, and Missouri.

Jurisdiction of the 8th Circuit Court of Appeals

The 8th Circuit Court of Appeals has jurisdiction over federal cases from the seven states within its boundaries. The court hears appeals from district courts within these states, as well as from administrative agencies and bankruptcy courts. The court also has jurisdiction over some criminal cases, including appeals from federal convictions in its seven-state region.

Notable cases heard by the 8th Circuit Court of Appeals

The 8th Circuit Court of Appeals has heard many notable cases throughout its history. Here are a few examples:

Roe v. Wade (1973)

In this landmark case, the 8th Circuit Court of Appeals ruled that a Texas law banning abortions was unconstitutional. The case was appealed to the Supreme Court, which upheld the 8th Circuit's ruling and established a woman's right to choose to have an abortion.

United States v. Nichols (1996)

This case involved the constitutionality of a Missouri law that allowed police officers to use deadly force to prevent the escape of a fleeing suspect. The 8th Circuit Court of Appeals ruled that the law was unconstitutional, citing the Fourth Amendment's protection against unreasonable seizures.

Planned Parenthood of Minnesota v. Rounds (2008)

In this case, the 8th Circuit Court of Appeals upheld a South Dakota law requiring doctors to inform patients seeking abortions that the procedure could increase their risk of suicide. The decision was controversial, with critics arguing that the law was based on flawed research and could discourage women from seeking abortions.

How cases are heard by the 8th Circuit Court of Appeals

Cases heard by the 8th Circuit Court of Appeals are typically appeals from district courts within the seven-state region. Parties that are dissatisfied with the outcome of their case in a lower court may file a notice of appeal with the 8th Circuit Court of Appeals. The court then reviews the record of the lower court proceedings, including transcripts of testimony and exhibits, and may hear oral arguments from the parties involved. After reviewing the case, the court issues a written opinion that explains its decision.

8th Circuit Court of Appeals Judges

The 8th Circuit Court of Appeals is composed of 11 judges who are appointed by the President of the United States and confirmed by the Senate. The current Chief Judge of the 8th Circuit is Lavenski R. Smith, who was appointed by President George W. Bush in 2002.

The 8th Circuit Court of Appeals is generally considered to be a conservative court, with a majority of its judges appointed by Republican presidents. However, the court's decisions are based on the law and legal precedent, rather than political ideology.

Conclusion

The 8th Circuit Court of Appeals plays an important role in the federal court system, hearing appeals from seven states in the Midwest. Over the years, the court has heard many important cases that have helped to shape the legal landscape in the United States.
